providers.title: The comparison theorem for projective resolutions
providers.scope: Chain maps from a projective augmented complex to an exact one exist over the identity and are unique up to chain homotopy. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: cd <= gd
providers.scope: The cellular chains of the universal cover of an n-dimensional classifying space form a free resolution of length n. Uses (CW).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A plane subgroup
providers.scope: A group containing Z^2 has cohomological dimension at least 2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A counterexample to the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There is a finitely generated residually finite group G with cd G = 2 and gd G = 3; proved in the last lesson from the named statements of the course.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Estimates for unit quaternions
providers.scope: Telescoping, the commutator estimate and invariance of the distance to 1 under inverses and conjugation. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Localized word-map degree (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A word map of H^m with nonsingular exponent matrix has nonzero degree on every conjugation-invariant open set containing the identity with no root on its boundary. Uses (DEG).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Moves that keep a basis
providers.scope: Adjoining a letter with a definition relator, changing free generators and shears preserve the basis property of a presentation. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Aspherical presentations
providers.scope: A group with a classifying space of dimension at most two has a presentation whose relator chains form a basis of the cycle module. Uses (HE), (CW).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The aligned presentation (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Such a group has a presentation with the basis property containing, for each word of a given cycle basis, a relator with the same chain, the other relators being controlled by letters of value 1. Uses (HE), (CW).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact counts
providers.scope: In an expression of a basis word as a product of conjugates of relators, the translated signed counts of the relators give exactly the basis vector of its distinguished relator. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The uniform quadratic estimate
providers.scope: With S-labels within epsilon of 1 and the ordinary relators of a finite set trivial, the product along a basis word differs from that along its distinguished relator by at most C(h + epsilon)h, uniformly on the group and its finite quotients. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A forbidden value
providers.scope: With epsilon <= eta, the supremum h of the distinguished products is never delta, and h <= 2C epsilon when h < delta. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite systems by degree
providers.scope: On a finite quotient, small prescribed S-labels extend to solutions of any finite set of ordinary relators with all distinguished products within delta of 1. Uses (DEG).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The comparison theorem (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If a residually finite group with a finite cycle basis of words has a classifying space of dimension at most two, small quaternion labellings with product 1 along the basis words have product 1 along every closed path. Uses (DEG), (HE), (CW).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deleting a vertex
providers.scope: A right-angled Artin group is the semidirect product of a free group on the cosets of the link subgroup with the group of the smaller graph. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Residual finiteness
providers.scope: Right-angled Artin groups and all their subgroups are residually finite. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cubes of the universal cover
providers.scope: The cubes of the universal cover of the torus complex are embedded, meet in common faces, and are locally finite. Uses (COV), (CUBE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Acyclicity of the cube complex
providers.scope: The cube complex of chains of a right-angled Artin group is a free resolution of Z. Uses (CUBE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cube complex is contractible
providers.scope: The universal cover of the torus complex is contractible, so its quotient by any subgroup is a classifying space of the same dimension. Uses (COV), (CUBE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ascending and descending links
providers.scope: The ascending and descending links of every vertex are barycentric subdivisions of L. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The level is acyclic
providers.scope: For a nonempty acyclic flag complex L, the zero level of the cube complex is connected and acyclic. Uses (SIMP).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The group and its cycle basis (OpenAI)
providers.scope: G is finitely generated by the edge letters, residually finite, cd G = 2, gd G <= 3, and the chains of the triangle words form a basis of the cycle module. Uses (SIMP), (CUBE), (COV).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An acyclic presentation complex
providers.scope: The presentation complex of <x, y | x^2 = y^5, x^2 = (xy^-1)^3> is acyclic. Uses (CELL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The seed representation
providers.scope: x -> u, y -> cos(pi/5) + v sin(pi/5) with u.v = 1/(2 sin(pi/5)) is a nontrivial homomorphism into the unit quaternions. Uses (PI1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The seed (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There is a finite acyclic flag complex of dimension two with a nontrivial homomorphism of its fundamental group into the unit quaternions. Uses (BARY), (CELL), (PI1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduced traces
providers.scope: Every element of a right-angled Artin group has a unique reduced trace, of length the word length. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplying by a generator
providers.scope: Right multiplication by a signed generator adjoins or deletes one maximal occurrence. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direction vectors move slowly
providers.scope: For g and gx different from 1, of lengths n and n + 1, the direction vectors lie in a common simplex and differ by at most 2/(n + 1) in the l^1 norm. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A slowly varying map of the level graph
providers.scope: The map of the level graph into L has edge images of diameter at most 4/N and triangle boundary images of diameter at most 8/N. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Commuting-power paths
providers.scope: Level paths through d a_q^-(N-j) a_r^-j map exactly onto the edge [q, r] of L, subdivided into N equal parts. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Small transport with nontrivial holonomy (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every epsilon > 0 the edges of the level complex carry quaternion labels within epsilon of 1 with product 1 around every triangle and a nontrivial product around some closed path. Uses (SC), (PI1), (COV).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
